title: Pompeii Wardrobe Opens After Almost 2,000 Years
paragraphs: It is a curious feature of Pompeii that its most affecting discoveries are rarely its grandest. The latest, announced by the Archaeological Park in late October 2026, is a wooden cupboard that stayed shut for almost two millennia in a house on the Via dell'Abbondanza, a thoroughfare that was among the city's busiest. The house, tentatively linked by inscriptions to a certain Cornelius Maximus, had its facade excavated as far back as 1912, yet the rooms behind it have only now yielded to scrutiny.

What emerged is a modest inventory of a life: a necklace of at least 24 tiny amulets in bone, glass paste, faience and rock crystal, evoking Mercury, Bes and miniature hands, feet, pine cones and grapes; 38 bronze coins, most from Nero's reign; tweezers, a scent bottle and an incense burner; and a box of lead weights hinting at a merchant's trade. Necklaces of this type were put on Roman children, so the piece may have belonged to a child of the household or been treasured by an adult long after childhood had passed.

It is tempting to read the scene as a snapshot of flight, with valuables abandoned at the moment Vesuvius erupted in 79, and researchers do entertain that possibility. But the evidence is circumstantial, and the park's director, Gabriel Zuchtriegel, has been admirably restrained: the residents' identities cannot be reconstructed with certainty, and whether they perished or escaped remains an open question. What the cupboard offers instead, in his words, is proof that Pompeii is “not just a place of great works of art”: its humblest relics restore the human dimension of the past.

questions.q: What makes the necklace hard to interpret?
questions.a: Such necklaces were worn by children, so it could be a child's or an adult's keepsake.

questions.q: Why is the 'snapshot of flight' reading only tempting, not proven?
questions.a: The evidence is circumstantial and the residents' fate and identity are unknown.

questions.q: What contrast does the opening sentence draw?
questions.a: Pompeii's most moving finds are rarely its grandest.
